title: TypeScript 7.1 Beta Released
tldr: TypeScript 7.1 Beta has been announced, introducing support for import attributes in ambient modules, source phase imports, and an updated target for ECMAScript 2026. These updates allow better handling of runtime-specific module types and preliminary support for proposed ECMAScript features.
bodyHtml:
Key points

  • Ambient module declarations now support import attributes to enforce runtime-expected attributes (such as type: 'css') and supply appropriate types.
  • Ambient module declarations matching import attributes are not validated against files on disk and are not included in built-in libraries.
  • Introduced source phase imports (import source x from ...) returning an AbstractModuleSource object before imports are linked or executed, primarily benefiting WebAssembly modules.
  • Added es2026 as a stable --target and --lib option, bringing declarations for Math.sumPrecise(), Iterator.concat(), and JSON methods.

Why it matters

Developers can now accurately type non-JavaScript file imports based on runtime module attributes rather than just file extensions. Additionally, source phase imports lay the groundwork for better WebAssembly and future JavaScript module instantiation workflows.

title: An Overview of CBOR and Its Characteristics
tldr: Concise Binary Object Representation (CBOR) is an IETF-standardized binary serialization format designed as an efficient alternative to JSON. It provides native binary data handling and smaller payload sizes while remaining self-describing.
bodyHtml:
Key points

  • CBOR supports the same data types as JSON while natively accommodating binary data without Base64 overhead.
  • The format uses header bytes to encode data types and sizes, enabling decoders to pre-allocate buffers and avoid escape sequences in UTF-8 text.
  • CBOR supports indefinite length collections and strings for streaming scenarios.
  • Unlike Protocol Buffers, CBOR is self-describing and does not require pre-shared schema files; compared to MessagePack, it is an IETF standard with streaming support.

Why it matters

CBOR offers a standardized, lightweight serialization format ideal for IoT and resource-constrained systems that need binary efficiency without the tight coupling of pre-shared schemas like Protocol Buffers.

title: Get Your .NET MAUI App Ready for Xcode 27
tldr: Apps built with Xcode 27 require adoption of UIKit's scene lifecycle to prevent crashes on launch. A new CLI-installed agent skill helps automate the migration across manifests, delegates, and custom lifecycle callbacks.
bodyHtml:
Key points

  • Every iOS app built using Xcode 27 must adopt the UIKit scene lifecycle using a scene delegate and Info.plist entries.
  • The requirement only affects builds made with Xcode 27; existing binaries compiled with earlier SDKs remain unaffected.
  • The maui-xcode27-migration agent skill can be installed via Microsoft.Maui.Cli preview to guide coding agents through the migration.
  • Projects targeting .NET 10 must update .NET MAUI packages to version 10.0.110 or higher to preserve features like App Actions and WebAuthenticator forwarding.
  • Custom application delegate logic, such as authentication callbacks, notification taps, and deep links, must be verified during migration.

Why it matters

Developers building .NET MAUI apps with Xcode 27 must update their scene lifecycle configuration to maintain app stability, authentication redirects, and platform integrations on iOS.

title: Bring Your Own Model to the GitHub Copilot SDK with C#
tldr: Developers can route GitHub Copilot SDK model inference to custom endpoints like Microsoft Foundry or Azure OpenAI using ProviderConfig. The approach retains the Copilot runtime and session orchestration while substituting the model provider.
bodyHtml:
Key points

  • The GitHub Copilot SDK decouples the agent orchestration runtime from model inference through ProviderConfig.
  • Supported destinations include Microsoft Foundry, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, and OpenAI-compatible endpoints like LiteLLM or vLLM.
  • Authentication supports both Microsoft Entra ID via AzureCliCredential and direct API keys.
  • Reasoning models may require adjusting MaxOutputTokens, as reasoning tokens count against the total output limit.
  • Sessions can be configured with tools, skills, and configuration discovery disabled for predictable testing.

Why it matters

This allows teams to use GitHub Copilot SDK's agent runtime while adhering to organizational model deployment, governance, and private infrastructure requirements.

title: Self-Hosting at Home With Cloudflare Tunnel
tldr: Cloudflare Tunnel enables hosting web applications on a home Linux server behind CGNAT without needing port forwarding or a public IP address.
bodyHtml:
Key points

  • The open-source cloudflared daemon establishes outbound encrypted connections to Cloudflare, bypassing CGNAT and dynamic IP limitations.
  • Routers can keep inbound ports closed, preventing direct public exposure of the origin server IP.
  • Traffic is terminated and decrypted at Cloudflare, requiring end-to-end security measures if trusting Cloudflare is a constraint.
  • Access can be secured using Cloudflare Access for private management, with alternatives like a VPS and WireGuard available for complete TLS passthrough.

Why it matters

It provides home-lab operators and developers an accessible way to expose internal web services and receive webhooks without ISP-level networking hurdles or exposed router ports.

title: Improving navigation experience in v0 with Next.js 16.4
tldr: Vercel used Next.js 16.4 Partial Prefetching and an agentic optimizer Skill to improve navigation performance across v0. The refactor prefetched reusable route parts and cached components while reducing unnecessary requests via user-intent prefetching.
bodyHtml:
Key points

  • Next.js 16.4 enables Cache Components and Partial Prefetching by default in create-next-app, allowing reusable route segments to load prior to a click.
  • The team used the next-partial-prefetching-optimizer Skill alongside an instant() Playwright test helper in an automated loop to verify UI availability before navigation.
  • Public template data was isolated from personalized viewer state and cached using 'use cache: remote', cacheLife(), and cacheTag().
  • To mitigate a 2.9x increase in prefetch requests in large grids, prefetching was updated to trigger on user intent (hover, focus, touch) instead of viewport entry.

Why it matters

The approach demonstrates how developers can combine Next.js Partial Prefetching, granular cache controls, and coding agents to achieve single-page app navigation speeds without ballooning prefetch network traffic.

title: Microsoft Releases .NET 9.0.21 Updates for ASP.NET Core and EF Core

bodyHtml:

  • Resolved an issue with HTTP/3 connection-level and stream-level abort locking.
  • Fixed a hang occurring in the SignalR Java client when reading an HTTP response body fails.
  • Updated third-party and internal dependencies including OpenApi 1.6.31, MessagePack 2.5.303, SQLitePCLRaw, and Azure Cosmos.

This maintenance release includes important protocol-level security and stability improvements for HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 handling in ASP.NET Core, along with bug fixes for multi-platform SignalR clients.

title: Analyzing Practical Use Cases for Durable Task in .NET
tldr: An architectural breakdown explores the practical implementation of durable execution using the Durable Task .NET SDK v1.26.0 and Durable Task Scheduler. The overview contrasts orchestrations with standard queues, focusing on resilient state and human-in-the-loop workflows.
bodyHtml:
Key points

  • Durable Task manages execution flow and resumption across interruptions using event-driven replay rather than saving CLR thread stacks.
  • Durable timers suspend processing without locking runtime threads, providing wait points for asynchronous external inputs like approvals.
  • Orchestration history handles coordination only; application logic remains authoritative for deduplication, state store reconciliation, and external side effects.

Why it matters

It clarifies the architectural boundary between framework-managed execution history and application-level idempotency when building complex distributed workflows or long-running tasks.

title: Implementing Multiple Authentication Schemes in ASP.NET Core
tldr: This guide demonstrates configuring multiple authentication schemes in an ASP.NET Core backend-for-frontend (BFF) application during an identity provider migration. It uses dynamic policy schemes and OpenID Connect token claims to determine which cookie scheme applies to a given request.
bodyHtml:
Key points

  • Uses AddPolicyScheme to dynamically select from four dedicated cookie schemes based on incoming request cookies, ensuring only one scheme executes per request.
  • Evaluates claims such as the identity provider claim in the OnTokenValidated event to sign users into the appropriate scheme.
  • Integrates with Duende IdentityServer using OpenID Connect code flow with PKCE, OAuth PAR, and client assertions.
  • Controllers are explicitly configured to authorize access using specific schemes or by allowing access via multiple schemes.

Why it matters

This architecture offers a transitional strategy for large applications migrating across identity providers or consolidating OIDC servers without immediately forcing a single default cookie scheme. It provides a blueprint for dynamically handling federated identity routing in ASP.NET Core.

title: Testing Time-Dependent Code in .NET Using TimeProvider and FakeTimeProvider
tldr: Developers can test time-sensitive logic in .NET 8+ by injecting TimeProvider and manipulating time with FakeTimeProvider. This eliminates real-time delays and allows precise evaluation of boundary conditions.
bodyHtml:
Key points

  • Replacing direct clock calls like DateTime.UtcNow with injected TimeProvider instances makes time a testable dependency.
  • FakeTimeProvider allows tests to advance simulated time programmatically, enabling precise boundary testing for expirations.
  • Passing TimeProvider to Task.Delay and CancellationTokenSource enables testing delays and timeouts instantly without real-world waiting.
  • Calls using real-time APIs like DateTime.UtcNow or unconfigured Task.Delay calls will bypass the fake provider and continue reading the system clock.

Why it matters

Relying on thread sleeps or short timeouts makes automated test suites slow and prone to timing flakiness. Built-in time abstraction support simplifies deterministic unit testing for expiring tokens, delays, and cancellation tokens.

title: C# Dev Kit 11.0 Re-Architected for Faster Loads and Lower Memory Usage

  • Introduces 'C# Doctor' to diagnose environment issues such as missing SDKs, missing runtimes, and package restore failures.

Why it matters

The structural overhaul significantly speeds up solution load and build times in VS Code, directly addressing latency and resource usage in large enterprise solutions.

title: Trimming Extra Dependencies in .NET NativeAOT via Linker Substitutions
tldr: Developers can use linker method substitutions in NativeAOT to strip unreachable code and reduce binary size when the compiler cannot statically determine unreachability.
bodyHtml:
Key points

  • Updating Microsoft.Diagnostics.Runtime (ClrMD) in a NativeAOT tool triggered an unexpected ~0.5MB size increase due to unused Azure.Identity and MSAL dependency chains.
  • The linker preserved these libraries because runtime string checks prevented static verification of dead code paths.
  • Using ILLink.Substitutions.xml allows developers to replace method bodies or property return values with constants to force dead-code elimination.
  • For NativeAOT builds, the substitution file must be explicitly passed via the --substitution compiler argument in IlcArg.

Why it matters

Provides a practical workaround for NativeAOT developers trying to maintain lightweight deployment binaries when third-party libraries introduce heavy, unneeded dependencies.

sources.title: Stripping extra dependencies in .NET NativeAOT apps using linker substitutions

title: Inside GitHub's Migration of the Copilot Runtime from TypeScript to Rust
tldr: GitHub migrated its Copilot agent runtime from TypeScript on Node.js to more than 800,000 lines of Rust using an incremental, agent-assisted process. The migration allows multi-language SDKs to load the runtime in-process via FFI, reducing latency and memory overhead.
bodyHtml:
Key points

  • The runtime migration was completed over 14.5 weeks using coding agents that consumed approximately $120,000 in tokens.
  • The migration used a strangler fig pattern across 128 pull requests, replacing TypeScript components incrementally while avoiding long-lived branches.
  • Rust was selected over .NET to provide a native C ABI without bringing an external garbage collector into foreign host processes like Go, Python, and the JVM.
  • Benchmarks showed out-of-process execution ran 3x to 6x faster, while in-process execution achieved 6x to 21x speedups with reduced memory consumption.

Why it matters

The project demonstrates a production-scale application of AI coding agents combined with the strangler fig architecture to perform major runtime rewrites without halting feature deployment.

sources.title: What It Actually Took to Port the GitHub Copilot Runtime to Rust

title: Using CSS @container Queries to Style Resizable Components
tldr: CSS container queries offer an alternative to viewport-based media queries by scoping styles to a parent element's dimensions. This resolves layout issues in dynamic, multi-pane, or resizable UI components.
bodyHtml:
Key points

  • Standard @media queries only evaluate the global viewport dimensions, which fails when individual sub-panels are resized independently.
  • @container queries evaluate conditions against a specified parent container instead of the whole browser window.
  • Implementation requires designating a parent container using properties such as container-name before writing conditional @container rules.
  • The approach enables responsive behavior for nested elements, such as hiding sidebars or reorganizing toolbars inside movable panes.

Why it matters

Component-driven web applications frequently place modular widgets or resizable splitters inside the layout. Container queries allow these elements to adapt cleanly to their allocated layout space without relying on custom JavaScript listeners.

title: Microsoft Updating NuGet Author-Signing Certificate
tldr: Microsoft will update its NuGet package author-signing certificate starting September 23, 2026. Developers enforcing trusted signer policies or verifying certificates must register the new SHA-256 fingerprint.
bodyHtml:
Key points

  • The new author-signing certificate transition takes effect on September 23, 2026.
  • New certificate SHA-256 fingerprint: 9A1B131BEE0605433056A4EA3815478A8E177961A968C6C0027C1093D1FEB630.
  • Systems enforcing NuGet client allow lists must add the new certificate via `dotnet nuget trust` or config updates, or package installation will fail with error NU3034.

Why it matters

Environments with strict package signature verification will fail to install newer Microsoft NuGet packages if client policies are not updated with the new certificate fingerprint.

title: Experimental Support for Device Bound Session Credentials in ASP.NET Core
tldr: ASP.NET Core in .NET 11 introduces experimental support for Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) to protect against session hijacking and cookie theft.
bodyHtml:
Key points

  • The Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.DeviceBoundSessions package acts as a drop-in hardening layer over existing cookie authentication schemes.
  • DBSC mitigates cookie theft by trading long-lived authentication cookies for short-lived cookies paired with hardware-bound refresh tokens.
  • Session refresh requests are validated by having the browser sign challenges using a private key isolated inside a hardware Trusted Platform Module (TPM).
  • Integrating DBSC with ASP.NET Core Identity requires manually wiring AddDeviceBoundSession to the IdentityConstants.ApplicationScheme.

Why it matters

DBSC significantly hardens web applications against credential exfiltration attacks by ensuring session cookies can only be refreshed from the original client hardware.

sources.title: Experimental support for Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) in ASP.NET Core: Exploring the .NET 11 preview - Part 8
